title: Artifact render job
description: One asynchronous artifact render on an `umbra serve` instance: what was asked for, how far it has got, and where the result will be. Returned by every `POST /artifacts/...` request that sets `"async": true` (202 while it runs, 200 when the content-addressed result was already cached) and by `GET /jobs/{id}`, which is what a client polls until `status` leaves `queued`/`running`. Produced by `umbra_py.serve.job_to_dict`. This is an HTTP-only document -- the CLI renders synchronously and has no jobs.

id.description: Opaque job identifier, unique within the running server. Job records are in-memory, so an id does not survive a restart -- the rendered artifact does, because it is a content-addressed file on disk, so a re-submitted request is answered from cache.

kind.description: Which artifact is being rendered -- the endpoint's own name.

status.description: Where the render has got to. `queued` and `running` mean poll again; `succeeded` means the `result` link resolves; `failed` means `error` says why and the result link is absent.

created.description: When the job was submitted (RFC 3339, UTC).

started.description: When the render began (RFC 3339, UTC), or null while the job is still queued. Also null for a job born `succeeded` from the cache, which ran no work at all.

finished.description: When the render finished or failed (RFC 3339, UTC), or null while it is queued or running.

links.description: Where to look next. A `self` link (this job document) is always present; a `result` link, typed with the artifact's own media type, is added exactly when `status` is `succeeded`.

rel.description: Link relation: `self` for this job document, `result` for the rendered artifact.

href.description: Absolute URL, resolved against the request's own base URL.

type.description: Media type of what the link points at: `application/json` for `self`, and for `result` the artifact's own type (`image/png`, `text/html; charset=utf-8`, or `application/json` for the stats endpoint).

title.description: Human-readable label, present on the `result` link.

cache.description: Present only when `status` is `succeeded`: whether the artifact was already on disk when the job was submitted (`hit`, no render ran) or was rendered for this job (`miss`). Its absence on a queued or running job is not a claim either way -- the answer is not known until the job finishes.

error.description: Present only when `status` is `failed`: the render's own message, in the words the synchronous request would have answered with.
